posts.title: Balancing Mung Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Balancing Mung Dal pairs split yellow mung with a separate onion-and-spice vagar.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.148
posts.body_markdown:
Balancing Mung Dal pairs split yellow mung with a separate onion-and-spice vagar, so the lentils stay simple while the topping brings the main aromatic character.

The dal simmers with ginger, turmeric, salt, oil, and an optional whole green chili until soft. Because split mung cooks quickly, the source keeps the base straightforward rather than building a long sauce.

The vagar is prepared separately with cumin, onion, ginger, salt, and optional chili, then spread over the cooked dal. Cilantro and tomato finish the dish just before serving.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups dried split yellow mung dal
- 5–6 cups water
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end, optional
- 1-inch piece fresh ginger, sliced
- 2 teaspoons salt
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon olive oil
- 1 tablespoon olive oil, or half ghee and half olive oil, for the vagar
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 3/4 cup onions, sliced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 fresh green chili, minced, optional
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish
- 1 tomato, sliced, for garnish

## Method
Combine the dal ingredients in a large pot and bring to a boil. Reduce to medium and simmer until cooked, about 20–25 minutes. For the vagar, heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat, add the cumin seeds, and let them sizzle about 30 seconds. Add the onions, ginger, salt, and optional chili, reduce to medium, and sauté until the onions are caramelized, about 7–8 minutes. Transfer the dal to a serving dish, spread the vagar over it, and garnish with cilantro and tomato. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: The King Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: The King Dal uses whole green mung beans rather than split dal, so the recipe begins with a long soak and has a firmer final texture.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.149
posts.body_markdown:
The King Dal uses whole green mung beans rather than split dal, so the recipe begins with a long soak and has a firmer final texture.

Mustard seeds are popped in oil before the soaked mung, hing, turmeric, optional cayenne, salt, and water are added. The source notes that longer soaking reduces both the cooking time and the amount of water required.

Lemon juice is stirred in after the beans are tender, and cilantro or parsley is used as the final garnish. The method stays focused on the beans rather than building a separate sauce.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup dried whole green mung beans
- 3 cups water, for soaking
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/4 teaspoon mustard seeds
- 1/8 teaspoon hing
- 2 cups water
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, optional
- Salt to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1 tablespoon fresh cilantro leaves or parsley, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Soak the mung beans in 3 cups water for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain. Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat, add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for about 30 seconds. Add the soaked beans, hing, 2 cups water, turmeric, optional cayenne, and salt. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook until tender, about 40–60 minutes, adding water if needed. Stir in the lemon juice, garnish with cilantro or parsley, and serve. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Sprouted Mung Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Sprouted Mung Dal is built around sprouted whole green mung beans, giving the dish a lighter structure than a thick split-lentil dal.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.150
posts.body_markdown:
Sprouted Mung Dal is built around sprouted whole green mung beans, giving the dish a lighter structure than a thick split-lentil dal.

The beans cook with turmeric, ginger, and optional whole green chili in a relatively small amount of water. The source cautions against overcooking and notes that the green husks begin to separate when the mung is ready.

After draining, the ginger and chili are removed. Lemon, optional cayenne, and salt are added only at the end so the final seasoning stays bright and direct.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups sprouted whole green mung beans
- 1 1/2 cups water
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 3 slices fresh ginger
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end, optional
- Juice of 1 lemon, optional
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, optional
- Salt to taste

## Method
Combine the sprouted mung beans, water, turmeric, ginger, and optional whole green chili in a large pot and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, adding a little water if the liquid dries too quickly. When the mung is tender and the green husks begin to loosen, drain the beans and remove the ginger and chili. Stir in the lemon juice, optional cayenne, and salt, then serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Granny’s Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Granny’s Dal uses whole urad dal and a separately cooked onion vagar, producing a substantial, earthy dish.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.151
posts.body_markdown:
Granny’s Dal uses whole urad dal and a separately cooked onion vagar, producing a substantial, earthy dish with a clear contrast between the soft lentils and caramelized topping.

The urad dal is soaked before simmering with salt, sliced ginger, oil, water, and an optional whole green chili. The source allows extra water during cooking if the pot begins to dry.

The vagar is deliberately simple: onion, ginger, chili, oil, and salt cooked until deeply caramelized. It is spooned over the finished dal just before serving, with optional cilantro on top.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups dried whole urad dal
- 6 cups water, for soaking
- 6 cups water, for cooking
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1-inch piece fresh ginger, sliced
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 5 cups water
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end, optional
- 2 teaspoons good oil, for the vagar
- 3/4 cup onions, sliced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2–2 fresh green chilies, minced
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, optional

## Method
Soak the urad dal for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain. Combine the soaked dal with the cooking water, salt, sliced ginger, oil, and optional whole chili in a large pot. Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low, and simmer until done, about 1 hour, adding water if needed. For the vagar, heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-low heat and sauté the onions, minced ginger, chilies, and salt until the onions are caramelized, about 8–10 minutes. Remove the ginger slices and whole chili from the dal, spoon the vagar over the top, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Strengthening Tur Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Strengthening Tur Dal is the source title for a layered tur dal finished with a tomato-and-spice vagar.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book pp.152–153
posts.body_markdown:
Strengthening Tur Dal is the source title for a layered tur dal finished with a tomato-and-spice vagar. This dal is substantial, but the presentation stays culinary rather than making health promises.

The tur dal is soaked briefly, simmered with turmeric, salt, hing, oil, and optional curry leaves, then kept separate while the vagar is prepared.

The vagar combines black mustard seeds, dried chilies, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, cayenne, tomato, and tomato purée. Lemon and optional sweetener are added after the vagar is folded into the dal.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups dried tur dal
- 6 cups water, for soaking
- 7 cups water, for cooking
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/8 teaspoon hing
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 4–6 curry leaves, optional
- 2 teaspoons good oil, for the vagar
- 2–3 dried red chilies
- 1 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- 1 cup tomatoes, chopped
- 2 tablespoons tomato purée
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon sweetener, optional
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves or parsley, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Soak the tur dal in 6 cups water for 1–2 hours, then drain. Combine the dal with 7 cups water in a large pot, bring to a boil, and skim away any froth. Add turmeric, salt, hing, oil, and optional curry leaves, then reduce to a simmer and cook about 45 minutes. For the vagar, heat the oil over medium-high heat, cook the dried chilies until darkened, then add the mustard seeds and let them pop under a lid for 30 seconds. Add the remaining vagar ingredients except lemon juice and sweetener and sauté 5–7 minutes. Stir the vagar into the dal, add lemon juice and optional sweetener, and simmer another 10 minutes. Garnish and serve. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Urad Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Urad Dal pairs cooked black-skinned urad with a rich tomato-and-onion vagar.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.154
posts.body_markdown:
Urad Dal pairs cooked black-skinned urad with a rich tomato-and-onion vagar. The dish is thicker and more robust than the lighter mung-based dals in the same section.

Cumin seeds start the vagar, followed by onion, ginger, garlic, tomato, coriander, green chili, and salt. The mixture cooks until the tomatoes soften and the aromatics come together.

Once the vagar is mixed into the cooked dal, garam masala and cilantro are added at the end. The source also offers an optional cream variation for a richer finish.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup dried urad dal
- 1 teaspoon ghee or butter
- 1 teaspoon olive oil or grapeseed oil
- 1 1/2 teaspoons whole cumin seeds
- 1 cup onions, minced
- 2 tablespoons fresh ginger, minced
- 4 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 3/4 cup tomatoes, diced
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 2 teaspoons ground coriander
- 1 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- Salt to taste
- 1 teaspoon garam masala, for garnish
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Soak and cook the urad dal using the source’s general bean-and-lentil method. Heat the ghee and oil in a pot or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds, cover, and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onions, ginger, garlic, tomatoes, salt, coriander, and green chilies, reduce to medium, and sauté for 5–7 minutes until the tomatoes are soft. Stir the vagar into the cooked dal, sprinkle with garam masala and cilantro, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Simple Brown Masoor Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Simple Brown Masoor Dal uses brown or green lentils, which cook quickly and keep more shape than red lentils when they are watched carefully.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.155
posts.body_markdown:
Simple Brown Masoor Dal uses brown or green lentils, which cook quickly and keep more shape than red lentils when they are watched carefully.

The lentils simmer with onion, tomato, ginger, oil, hing, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, chili, and salt in one pot. The source specifically cautions against overcooking.

Sweetener and lemon are stirred in only after the lentils are tender, creating a gentle sweet-sour finish. Cilantro is scattered over the top just before serving.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup dried brown or green lentils
- 3 cups water or vegetable stock
- 1/3 cup onions, chopped
- 3/4 cup tomatoes, chopped
- 1 teaspoon tomato purée, optional
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- Pinch of hing, optional
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 3/4 teaspoon ground cumin
- 3/4 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/4 teaspoon fresh green chilies, chopped, or cayenne
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 teaspoon gur or other sweetener
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Bring the lentils and water or stock to a boil in a medium pot. Add the onions, tomatoes, optional tomato purée, ginger, oil, optional hing, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, chili, and salt. Reduce to a simmer and cook for about 20 minutes, adding water if necessary, until the lentils are tender but not mushy. Stir in the gur and lemon juice until the sweetener dissolves, adjust the seasoning, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 2–3 servings.

posts.title: Quick & Easy Red Masoor Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Quick & Easy Red Masoor Dal | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Quick & Easy Red Masoor Dal is a one-pot red-lentil recipe designed around the speed of masoor, which needs no soaking and softens in about twenty minutes.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.156
posts.body_markdown:
Quick & Easy Red Masoor Dal is a one-pot red-lentil recipe designed around the speed of masoor, which needs no soaking and softens in about twenty minutes.

The lentils cook with salt, optional hing, ginger, whole green chili, tomato, onion, and turmeric. Froth is skimmed as the pot comes to a simmer.

Lemon and optional gur or maple syrup are added after the lentils are cooked. Cilantro is used at serving, giving the simple dal a fresh final note.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup dried red lentils
- 3 cups water
- 1 teaspoon salt
- Pinch of hing, optional
- 3 slices fresh ginger
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end
- 1/2 cup tomatoes, diced
- 1 teaspoon tomato purée, optional
- 1/2 cup onions, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/2 teaspoon gur or maple syrup, optional
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

## Method
Combine all ingredients except turmeric, lemon juice, optional sweetener, and cilantro in a large pot and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and skim away any froth that rises. Stir in the turmeric and cook until the lentils are done, about 20 minutes, adding water if the dal becomes too dry. Add the lemon juice and optional gur or maple syrup, stirring until dissolved, then garnish with cilantro and serve. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Channa Dal
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Channa Dal uses split chickpeas with a strongly seasoned tomato vagar. The cooked dal stays separate until the sauce has fully developed.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.157
posts.body_markdown:
Channa Dal uses split chickpeas with a strongly seasoned tomato vagar. The cooked dal stays separate until the sauce has fully developed.

Cumin seeds are heated first, then tomato, coriander, turmeric, garlic, ginger, green chili, salt, and tomato paste are sautéed until the tomatoes soften and the spices are cooked through.

The vagar is folded into the cooked channa dal and simmered briefly before lemon and maple syrup are added. Cilantro finishes the dish.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups dried split chickpeas
- 2 tablespoons good oil
- 1 1/2 teaspoons whole cumin seeds
- 1 1/2 cups fresh tomatoes, chopped
- 1 1/2 teaspoons ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1–2 teaspoons fresh ginger, minced
- Salt to taste
- 1–2 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced, or cayenne
- 2 tablespoons tomato paste
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup or other sweetener
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice, or to taste
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Soak and cook the split chickpeas using the source’s general bean-and-lentil method. Heat the oil in a medium frying pan over medium-high heat, add the cumin seeds, and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, garlic, ginger, salt, chili, and tomato paste. Reduce to medium and sauté for 8–10 minutes, until the tomatoes soften and the spices are well cooked. Stir the vagar into the cooked channa dal and cook 5 minutes more. Add the lemon juice and maple syrup, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Ameeta’s Sliced Tofu with Green Onions & Cilantro
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Ameeta's Sliced Tofu with Green Onions & Cilantro | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Ameeta’s Sliced Tofu with Green Onions & Cilantro is a chilled marinated tofu dish rather than a cooked curry.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.158
posts.body_markdown:
Ameeta’s Sliced Tofu with Green Onions & Cilantro is a chilled marinated tofu dish rather than a cooked curry, so the dressing does most of the flavor work.

The tofu is drained and dried before slicing. Soy sauce or Bragg seasoning, ginger, sesame oil, Dijon, and lemon are shaken together and used as the marinade.

After at least thirty minutes, cilantro, green onion, sesame seeds, and optional chili flakes are added. The final dish is tossed gently and served without further cooking.

## Ingredients
- 1 package firm tofu, about 1 1/2 cups
- 1 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1/2 cup green onions, sliced
- 2 tablespoons sesame seeds
- 1/4 teaspoon dried red chili flakes, optional
- 1/4 cup soy sauce or Bragg seasoning
- 2 tablespoons fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- 1/4 cup lemon juice

## Method
Drain the tofu, wrap it in a dish towel, and let it dry. Shake the soy sauce or Bragg seasoning, ginger, sesame oil, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice together in a jar. Slice the tofu about 1/2 inch thick, place it in a medium bowl, and pour the dressing over it. Marinate for at least 30 minutes. Add the cilantro, green onions, sesame seeds, and optional chili flakes, toss gently, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Coconut Vegetable Tofu Medley
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Coconut Vegetable Tofu Medley combines peppers, zucchini, tofu, and coconut milk.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.159
posts.body_markdown:
Coconut Vegetable Tofu Medley combines peppers, zucchini, tofu, and coconut milk in a quick stovetop dish that keeps the vegetables distinct rather than stewing them for a long time.

Onion is softened first, then garlic, ginger, turmeric, salt, and chili are cooked briefly. The peppers and zucchini go in next and are covered until nearly tender.

Tofu and coconut milk are added only near the end, along with lemon and optional agave or maple syrup. Cilantro provides the final fresh garnish.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 1/3 cup onions, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 fresh green chili, minced
- 1 cup red bell peppers, diced
- 1 cup yellow bell peppers, diced
- 3 cups zucchini, quartered and sliced
- 2 cups medium tofu, cubed
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1 teaspoon agave nectar or maple syrup, optional
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions and sauté for 1–2 minutes. Reduce to medium, add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, salt, and chili, and cook another 1–2 minutes. Add the peppers and zucchini, cover, and cook for 4–6 minutes until almost tender. Add the tofu, coconut milk, lemon juice, and optional sweetener. Reduce to medium-low and simmer 5 minutes more. Garnish with cilantro and serve. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Let’s Tofu with Bok Choy & Yam Home Fries
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Let's Tofu with Bok Choy & Yam Home Fries | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Let’s Tofu with Bok Choy & Yam Home Fries is really two quick preparations served together: sauced tofu with bok choy and separately browned yam slices.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.160
posts.body_markdown:
Let’s Tofu with Bok Choy & Yam Home Fries is really two quick preparations served together: sauced tofu with bok choy and separately browned yam slices.

The tofu is browned first, then thickened with an arrowroot slurry, soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Bok choy is added only after the sauce begins to thicken.

The yams cook in a second pan, where they are browned, briefly covered with water, and then uncovered so the remaining moisture can evaporate. Both parts are served immediately.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil
- 1 cup medium-firm tofu, cubed
- 1/2 teaspoon ground arrowroot
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 teaspoon soy sauce
- 1/2 teaspoon oyster sauce
- 1 cup bok choy, chopped
- 1 teaspoon ghee or good oil
- 1 cup yams, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick
- Water, enough to cover the yams in the skillet

## Method
Heat the sesame oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and brown the tofu for about 2 minutes. Dissolve the arrowroot in 1/4 cup water and add it with the soy sauce and oyster sauce, stirring constantly as the mixture comes to a boil and thickens, about 1 minute. Add the bok choy, cover, reduce to medium, and cook 3–5 minutes. In another frying pan, heat the ghee or oil over high heat, brown the yam slices on both sides, then add enough water to cover them. Cover and cook 4 minutes, uncover, and continue until most of the water evaporates. Serve the yams with the tofu and bok choy. Makes 2 servings.

posts.title: Tandoori Tofu
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Tandoori Tofu depends on an overnight yogurt marinade, allowing the tofu to take on ginger, garlic, lemon, spices, chili, and cilantro.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.161
posts.body_markdown:
Tandoori Tofu depends on an overnight yogurt marinade, allowing the tofu to take on ginger, garlic, lemon, spices, chili, and cilantro before it reaches the oven.

The marinade combines yogurt with cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and fresh aromatics. The long resting time is the main preparation step.

The tofu is broiled in a single layer and stirred so the pieces brown on more than one side. Fresh cilantro is added only after cooking.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 cups firm tofu, cubed
- 1 cup plain yogurt
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 fresh green chili, minced
- 1/4–1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- 3/4 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Combine the tofu with the yogurt, garlic, ginger, cilantro, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, turmeric, green chili, garam masala, and salt in a large bowl. Toss until well coated, cover, and refrigerate overnight. Set the oven to broil and spread the tofu in a single layer on a baking sheet, pouring any remaining marinade over the top. Broil on the upper rack, stirring so the pieces brown lightly on multiple sides, about 3–4 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: The Modern “Pau” Baji
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: The Modern "Pau" Baji uses texturized vegetable protein as the main protein, mixing it with yogurt, eggs, herbs, aromatics, and vegetables.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.162
posts.body_markdown:
The Modern “Pau” Baji uses texturized vegetable protein as the main protein, mixing it with yogurt, eggs, herbs, aromatics, and vegetables in a highly seasoned skillet dish.

The TVP is first reconstituted in hot vegetable stock, then combined with onion, cilantro, chili, ginger, garlic, dhanna jeera, lemon, salt, yogurt, and eggs.

A mustard-seed tempering starts the cooking stage, followed by celery, carrot, bell pepper, zucchini, and finally the TVP mixture. The pan is cooked until the excess moisture is absorbed.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups texturized vegetable protein
- 2 cups hot vegetable stock
- 1/2 cup onions, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 fresh green chili, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon dhanna jeera
- 4 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 cup plain yogurt
- 2 eggs
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 2 dried red chilies
- 1 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 1/4 cup celery, chopped
- 1/2 cup carrots, chopped
- 1/2 cup red bell peppers, diced
- 1/2 cup zucchini, sliced and quartered

## Method
Soak the TVP in the hot vegetable stock for about 10 minutes, until reconstituted. Mix it with the onions, cilantro, green chili, ginger, garlic, dhanna jeera, lemon juice, salt, yogurt, and eggs. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat, add the dried red chilies, and cook until darkened, 1–2 minutes. Add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the celery and carrots and sauté 3–4 minutes, then add the bell peppers and zucchini. When the pan begins to dry, add the TVP mixture and cook about 5 minutes more, until the moisture is absorbed. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Vegetarian Mixed Bean Chili
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Vegetarian Mixed Bean Chili combines cooked mixed beans with texturized vegetable protein, vegetables, tomato, and chili seasoning in a one-pot meal.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.163
posts.body_markdown:
Vegetarian Mixed Bean Chili combines cooked mixed beans with texturized vegetable protein, vegetables, tomato, and chili seasoning in a one-pot meal.

The TVP is separately reconstituted in hot water with vegetable bouillon while onion, celery, and carrot begin cooking in the pot. Garlic, mushrooms, and peppers are added next.

Tomatoes, beans, chili seasoning, optional wine, optional oyster sauce or sweetener, and hot sauce finish the mixture. The chili then simmers long enough for the TVP to absorb the surrounding flavors.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup texturized vegetable protein
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 cup hot water
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1 cup onions, chopped in large pieces
- 1 cup celery, chopped
- 1 cup carrots, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup mushrooms, chopped
- 1 1/2 cups mixed green, yellow, and red bell peppers, cubed
- 1 1/2 cups tomatoes, chopped
- 1 1/2 cups mixed cooked beans
- 1 tablespoon chili con carne seasoning
- 1 tablespoon wine, optional
- 1 tablespoon oyster sauce, maple syrup, or honey, optional
- Dash of hot chili sauce
- Salt to taste

## Method
Combine the TVP, bouillon powder, and hot water in a medium bowl and let stand 10 minutes. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat, add the onions, celery, and carrots, and sauté 3–4 minutes. Add the garlic, mushrooms, and peppers and cook 2 minutes more. Add the tomatoes, beans, chili seasoning, optional wine, optional oyster sauce or sweetener, hot sauce, and reconstituted TVP. Simmer about 20 minutes, taste, and add salt if necessary. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Happy Cow Shepherd’s Pie
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Happy Cow Shepherd’s Pie replaces the usual meat layer with seasoned texturized vegetable protein and vegetables.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.164
posts.body_markdown:
Happy Cow Shepherd’s Pie replaces the usual meat layer with seasoned texturized vegetable protein and vegetables, then tops the filling with mashed sweet potato.

The TVP is reconstituted first, then cooked with onion, ginger, garlic, chili, celery, bell pepper, peas, mushrooms, herbs, tomato, and seasoning until the filling is thick enough for a casserole.

Mashed sweet potato is spread over the cooked filling and scored with a fork before a small amount of Parmesan is added. The assembled pie is baked until heated through.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 cup hot water
- 1 cup texturized vegetable protein
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/3 cup onions, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end
- 1 celery stalk, thinly sliced
- 1/2 bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 cup fresh green peas, cooked
- 1/4 cup mushrooms, sliced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves or parsley
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon oil
- Freshly ground black pepper to taste
- 1/2 cup tomato sauce or chopped fresh tomatoes
- 3 sweet potatoes, cooked and mashed, about 5 cups
- 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese

## Method
Dissolve the bouillon in the hot water, add the TVP, and let it stand for 5 minutes. Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat, add the onions, ginger, garlic, and chili, and sauté for 2 minutes. Add the TVP and all remaining ingredients except the mashed sweet potatoes and Parmesan. Reduce to medium and simmer about 20 minutes, covering if the filling starts to dry. Remove the chili. Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C), spread the TVP mixture in a casserole dish, cover with mashed sweet potatoes, rake the surface with a fork, sprinkle with Parmesan, and bake 20 minutes. Cut into squares and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Vegetarian Kheema Matur
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Vegetarian Kheema Matur uses texturized vegetable protein in place of ground meat, pairing it with peas, tomato, warm spices, and whole aromatics.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.165
posts.body_markdown:
Vegetarian Kheema Matur uses texturized vegetable protein in place of ground meat, pairing it with peas, tomato, warm spices, and whole aromatics.

The TVP is reconstituted in vegetable bouillon before the cooking begins. Onion, garlic, ginger, and green chili form the base, followed by tomato, tomato paste, cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, cinnamon, and cardamom.

The TVP and peas are simmered with water until the mixture is cohesive. Lemon juice and cilantro are added at the end after the whole spices are removed.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 cup boiling water
- 1 cup texturized vegetable protein
- 3 teaspoons grapeseed oil or good oil
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- 3/4 cup tomatoes, diced
- 2 teaspoons tomato paste
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- 2 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 cup fresh green peas
- 1 cup water
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves or parsley, chopped

## Method
Dissolve the bouillon in the boiling water, add the TVP, and let stand 10 minutes. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat, add the onions, garlic, ginger, and chilies, and sauté until the onions soften, about 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, cinnamon, cardamom, and salt and cook about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes soften and oil begins to show at the surface. Add the TVP, peas, and water and cook 10 minutes more. Stir in the lemon juice, remove the cinnamon and cardamom, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Cumin Rice
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Cumin Rice is one of the simplest rice dishes in the source, using whole cumin seeds to perfume basmati without turning it into a heavily seasoned pilau.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.167
posts.body_markdown:
Cumin Rice is one of the simplest rice dishes in the source, using whole cumin seeds to perfume basmati without turning it into a heavily seasoned pilau.

The cumin seeds are heated briefly in oil before the rice, water, and salt are added. That short contact with hot oil brings out the spice’s aroma before the pot is covered.

The rice then cooks entirely by absorption under a tight lid. There are no additional vegetables or garnishes, so the grain remains the focus.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 1/4 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1 cup basmati rice
- 2 cups water
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste

## Method
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the basmati rice, water, and salt and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover tightly, and cook for 20 minutes. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Aromatic Basmati Rice
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Aromatic Basmati Rice cooks the rice directly with whole cloves, cardamom, peppercorns, and cinnamon bark.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.168
posts.body_markdown:
Aromatic Basmati Rice cooks the rice directly with whole cloves, cardamom, peppercorns, and cinnamon bark, allowing the grains to absorb the spice aroma as they steam.

Unlike a pilau, there is no sautéing stage. Everything goes into the pot together, making the method simple even though the flavor comes from several whole spices.

The source notes that the whole spices may be removed before serving or left in for appearance and continued aroma, but diners should not eat them.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup white basmati rice
- 2 cups water
- 2 cloves
- 3 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 4 whole peppercorns
- 2 pieces cinnamon bark, 1–2 inches long
- Salt to taste

## Method
Combine the basmati rice, water, cloves, cardamom, peppercorns, cinnamon bark, and salt in a medium pot over high heat. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes. Remove the whole spices before serving if desired. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Saffron Rice
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Saffron Rice uses only a few saffron strands, but the spice is soaked first so its color and aroma disperse through the entire pot.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.169
posts.body_markdown:
Saffron Rice uses only a few saffron strands, but the spice is soaked first so its color and aroma disperse through the entire pot.

The soaked saffron and its water are combined with basmati rice, fresh water, and salt. The rice then cooks by the same covered absorption method used elsewhere in the source.

The source also suggests optional raisins, dried cranberries, or toasted slivered almonds. These are variations rather than part of the base recipe.

## Ingredients
- 4 saffron strands
- 2 tablespoons water, for soaking
- 1 cup basmati rice
- 2 cups water
- Salt to taste

## Method
Soak the saffron strands in 2 tablespoons water for 15 minutes. Transfer the saffron and its soaking water to a medium pot with the basmati rice, 2 cups water, and salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Kitchari
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Kitchari combines split mung dal and basmati rice in a deliberately soft preparation.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.170
posts.body_markdown:
Kitchari combines split mung dal and basmati rice in a deliberately soft preparation. The source treats the slightly mushy texture as part of the dish rather than a sign of overcooking.

The rice and dal cook together in water with salt, making this one of the most stripped-back recipes in the section. Oil, ghee, or butter is added after cooking rather than used to start the pot.

The source gives optional turmeric or whole-spice variations and suggests extra water and time for an even softer texture. Those additions are not required for the base version.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 cup split mung dal
- 1/2 cup basmati rice
- 2 cups water
- Salt to taste
- 2 teaspoons flax oil, hemp oil, ghee, or butter

## Method
Combine the split mung dal, basmati rice, water, and salt in a medium pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 25–30 minutes. Drizzle with the oil, ghee, or butter just before serving. For a softer texture, add about 1/2 cup more water and cook a few minutes longer. Makes 2–3 servings.

posts.title: Organic Brown Rice Kitchari
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Organic Brown Rice Kitchari adapts the rice-and-mung combination to short-grain brown rice, so it needs a longer cooking time than the basmati version.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.171
posts.body_markdown:
Organic Brown Rice Kitchari adapts the rice-and-mung combination to short-grain brown rice, so it needs a longer cooking time than the basmati version.

The brown rice and split mung dal cook together with water, salt, and optional turmeric. There is no separate sautéing stage or spice tempering in the base recipe.

After cooking, the covered pot rests briefly before oil, ghee, or butter is drizzled over the top. The source also notes that the mung dal can be soaked in advance if time allows.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup organic short-grain brown rice
- 1/4 cup split mung dal
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, optional
- 2 cups water
- 2 teaspoons flax oil, hemp oil, ghee, or butter

## Method
Combine the brown rice, split mung dal, salt, optional turmeric, and water in a medium pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 45 minutes. Remove from the heat and let the pot stand covered for 5 minutes. Drizzle with the oil, ghee, or butter before serving. Makes 2–3 servings.

posts.title: Vegetable Rice Pilau
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Vegetable Rice Pilau is a full one-pot rice dish where basmati cooks with potato, tomato, bell pepper, peas, carrot, and spices.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.172
posts.body_markdown:
Vegetable Rice Pilau is a full one-pot rice dish where basmati cooks with potato, tomato, bell pepper, peas, carrot, and spices rather than having vegetables folded in afterward.

Cumin seeds are heated first, followed by onion, garlic, and ginger. The rice is briefly coated in oil before the vegetables and turmeric are added.

Vegetable bouillon and enough additional water to cover the rice complete the pot. The pilau cooks covered until the rice and vegetables are tender, then fresh herbs are added.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 cup hot water
- 1 tablespoon oil
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cups white basmati rice
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end
- 1 cup potatoes, cubed
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1/2 cup red bell peppers, cubed
- 1 cup fresh green peas
- 3/4 cup carrots, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley or cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Dissolve the bouillon powder in the hot water and set aside. Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat, add the cumin seeds, and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onions, garlic, and ginger and sauté 30 seconds. Add the rice and stir until coated with oil, then add the chili, potatoes, tomato, bell pepper, peas, carrots, turmeric, and salt. Pour in the bouillon mixture and enough additional water to cover the rice by about 1 inch. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook about 20–25 minutes. Remove the chili, mix gently, garnish with parsley or cilantro, and serve. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Simple Pea Pilau
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Simple Pea Pilau is a compact basmati dish with peas and optional whole spices.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.173
posts.body_markdown:
Simple Pea Pilau is a compact basmati dish with peas and optional whole spices, giving the rice more character without turning it into a vegetable-heavy pilau.

Cumin seeds are heated briefly in oil before the rice, peas, seasonings, and water are added. Peppercorns, cinnamon bark, and cardamom are optional.

The rice cooks covered for twenty minutes. The whole spices are removed before serving so only their aroma remains in the finished dish.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1/2 cup white basmati rice
- 1/2 cup fresh green peas
- 2 peppercorns, optional
- 1 piece cinnamon bark, about 1 inch long, optional
- 1 cardamom pod, slit at the end, optional
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, optional
- 1 1/4 cups water

## Method
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the basmati rice, peas, optional peppercorns, optional cinnamon, optional cardamom, salt, optional turmeric, and water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes. Remove any whole spices before serving. Makes 2–3 servings.

posts.title: Bean Pilau
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Bean Pilau combines cooked azuki beans with basmati rice, yogurt, tomato, whole spices, and aromatics in a single pot.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.174
posts.body_markdown:
Bean Pilau combines cooked azuki beans with basmati rice, yogurt, tomato, whole spices, and aromatics in a single pot, making it more substantial than a plain rice side.

Onions are cooked until golden first, then tomato, yogurt, garlic, ginger, chili, cilantro, coriander, cumin, cloves, peppercorns, cardamom, cinnamon, and salt are sautéed until the tomato softens.

The cooked beans and uncooked rice are stirred into that seasoned base. Water is added to cover the rice, and the pilau cooks covered before resting off the heat.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon grapeseed oil or other good oil
- 1 cup onions, thinly sliced
- 1 1/2 cups tomatoes, chopped
- 1 cup plain yogurt
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 teaspoons fresh green chilies
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 3 cloves
- 4 peppercorns
- 3 cardamom pods, slit at the end, optional
- 2 cinnamon sticks, 1–2 inches long
- Salt to taste
- 2 cups azuki beans, cooked
- 2 cups basmati rice
- Water, enough to cover the rice by about 1 inch

## Method
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the onions and cook until golden, about 4–5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, yogurt, garlic, ginger, chilies, cilantro, coriander, cumin, cloves, peppercorns, optional cardamom, cinnamon, and salt and sauté for 7–8 minutes, until the tomatoes soften. Stir in the cooked azuki beans and basmati rice. Add enough water to cover the rice by about 1 inch, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20–25 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand for 5 minutes. Remove the whole spices before serving. Makes 6–8 servings.
